title: Chelsea criticised for transfer decision that has helped rivals
description: Kai Havertz at Arsenal Raises Fresh Questions Over Chelsea Transfer StrategyKai Havertz came back to hurt Chelsea again, and that is the part that matters. Arsenal’s 2-1 win over their London rivals...
fullText:
Kai Havertz came back to hurt Chelsea again, and that is the part that matters. Arsenal's 2-1 win over their London rivals was shaped by a player Chelsea once had, then chose to move on. When that player delivers in a game of this size, the debate writes itself.

Joe Cole did not dress it up. He criticised Chelsea for letting a top-level talent leave and strengthen a direct rival. His description of Havertz as "world-class" cuts to the point. If that is the level of player you believe he is, selling him across the city looks careless. Selling him to a team chasing major honours looks worse.

Havertz was instrumental in Arsenal securing the 2-1 result, and that will sting at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea have spent heavily and churned through players, yet this is the sort of move that keeps coming back. Clubs can talk about squad balance, tactical fit and long-term planning, but football is ruthless. If the player thrives elsewhere, especially at a rival, the explanation sounds thin.

There is a broader issue here with Chelsea's transfer strategy. Talent has left, money has gone out, and clarity has often been missing. Havertz may not have been perfect at Chelsea, few were during a chaotic period, but quality was always obvious. Arsenal saw a player they could use. Chelsea saw one they could cash in on. Right now, Arsenal look smarter.

Mikel Arteta deserves credit for finding a role and structure that brings out Havertz's strengths. Arsenal have been more coherent, more settled and more demanding. That gives good players a platform. Chelsea, by contrast, are still wrestling with identity. Until that changes, stories like this will keep surfacing.

The uncomfortable truth is simple. Chelsea sold quality to a rival, and that rival has benefited. In elite football, those mistakes do not fade quietly.

title: Arsenal vs. Chelsea match thread: old friends meet in a London derby
description: Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates in the first clash between traditional big four (or five, or six, however you want to phrase it) clubs of the Premier League season. In life, you’re either a red or a blue. Arsenal vs. Chelsea is about as red vs. blue as they come.
fullText:
Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates in the first clash between traditional big four (or five, or six, however you want to phrase it) clubs of the Premier League season. In life, you're either a red or a blue. Arsenal vs. Chelsea is about as red vs. blue as they come. This will be the first meeting between Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso, notable because the pair are lifelong friends. They played on teams growing up together in Spain.

Both clubs have two wins from two to start the season. Arsenal have done it with organization and defense, as you'd expect. They've not conceded a goal from either match (Hull City haven't conceded from three). Chelsea's attack has started the season quickly with seven goals scored from their opening two matches. They've also conceded five over those games, looking particularly vulnerable to crosses and set pieces.

Many expected new manager Xabi Alonso to setup his side to have plenty of the ball, as he did in previous coaching stops. In last weekend's 4-3 win over Brighton, Chelsea had 25% possession and completed just over 200 passes to Brighton's 590. The Blues attack quickly and directly. I'll be interested to see how they match up against Arsenal's more robust defense and organization.

Arsenal are unbeaten in 11 straight matches in all competitions against Chelsea (8-3-0). The Blues last win against the Gunners came in August 2022. There will be just two players starting for their same teams from the starting lineups that day — Reece James and Bukayo Saka. Kai Havertz is also likely to start but, as we know, switched sides in the interim. The Arsenal lineup from that match, woo boy — Leno, Cedric, Holding, Mari, Tierney, Xhaka, Lokonga, Saka, Smith Rowe, Pepe, Martinelli.

I'll be keeping a close watch on Bukayo Saka, who has scored in both matches this season for Arsenal but has a pretty dismal record against Chelsea. He'll no longer be running at Marc Cucurella, who like him or not, rate him or not, always did well keeping Saka quiet. Chelsea's defense has looked unorganized way more often than Xabi Alonso would like, so if there ever was a time for Bukayo to improve his output against the Blues, it'd be today.

Arsenal will be without William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, who remain out with the back and groin problems that have kept him out all season. The Dutch fullback is getting closer to making his return. Cristhian Mosquera, who was withdrawn against Aston Villa as a precaution per Mikel Arteta, looks like he'll miss out today. Bruno Guimaraes has been dealing with a groin issue and reportedly picked up an additional knock on the training ground this week but was with the squad for Sunday's pre-match walk. Declan Rice was a surprise miss from said walk. He trained all week, including yesterday, so his absence is particularly odd. UPDATE: Declan Rice starts today, he's fine.

For Chelsea, Moises Caicedo faces a late fitness test to determine his availability. He made a brief appearance as a substitute last week. New signing Marco Palestra, who played plenty in the preseason, has yet to make his Premier League debut for the club because of a knock. His status is up in the air / doubtful. Striker Emmanuel Emegha, who also joined the club this summer, is out with a hamstring issue. Jordan Henderson is still recovering from the broken arm / wrist he suffered at the World Cup after falling during a celebration.

title: McColgan wins London Big Half after five months out
description: Britain's Eilish McColgan returns to competitive action after five months out with a broken toe to win the London Big Half for a fourth time.
fullText:
Eilish McColgan claimed her fourth victory at the Big Half in London on Sunday after returning to action following five months out with a fractured foot.

The 35-year-old Scot suffered the injury during the London Marathon in April, crossing the line in seventh place with blood seeping through her shoe, and was forced to pull out of July's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

But McColgan showed the benefit of months of warm weather training, completing a comfortable victory over the 13.1-mile course back in the English capital.

The British women's half-marathon record holder beat last year's winner Jessica Warner-Judd by one minute 19 seconds, finishing in a time of 1hr 10mins 54secs.

McColgan might have 'one more' Games in her

McColgan to miss Glasgow Games defence after foot fracture

It was more than three minutes outside her best time for the course and well outside her British record for the distance of 1:05:43.

Britain's Jack Rowe missed out on a record fourth consecutive victory in the men's race, finishing in second place, 14 seconds behind Birchfield Harriers' Kadar Omar Abdullahi, who won in a time of 1:01:51.

Britain's David Weir defended his title in the men's wheelchair event, winning the race for the fifth time in its nine-year history in a new record time.

The 47-year-old, who retired from Paralympic competition in 2024, knocked 45 seconds off his own record for the course, which he set last year, winning in 46:13.

Eden Rainbow Cooper won the women's event in 52:47 to defend her title.

fullText:
Previewing Chelsea's Premier League clash against Arsenal.

Jorrel Hato is relishing Chelsea's Premier League clash against Arsenal on Sunday afternoon.

Chelsea head to the Emirates to face the current champions, looking to end a run of four straight away league defeats to Mikel Arteta's side.

After his summer appointment, Xabi Alonso is hoping to claim a first away league win against the Gunners since 2021, when Chelsea claimed a 2-0 victory.

It's been a positive start to Chelsea's campaign, with wins over Fulham and Brighton and Hove Albion in their opening league matches. Hato has started both league games, with the summer arrival Pep Chavarria still settling into his new surroundings in west London.

The 20-year-old will be keen to keep his place in the side with a start against Arsenal.

Chelsea's toughest test of the season awaits. Their record against the so-called 'big six' away from home has been problematic in recent years.

Whether they're ready to be title challengers yet remains to be seen and that will be established in the coming months. But given the recruitment and start the Blues have made, they are certainly heading in a positive direction.

A win at the Emirates would not only continue the perfect start to the season in terms of points, making it three wins from three, it would signify a statement of intent and sign of change, as they overcome their biggest hurdle - not losing against the Gunners, who they used to have so much joy against.

That's the aim for Chelsea. To show improvement against Arsenal, and if they can manage a clean sheet - that is a huge bonus.

Arsenal are yet to concede this season, so Chelsea will have their work cut out. Patience and ruthlessness in box boxes will be key.

Preparations are almost done, and Hato has warned Arsenal of the danger Chelsea will pose.

Previewing the trip to the Emirates, Hato told the club's in-house media: "We look at things game by game. I think we had a great start. We spoke with each other and said: 'Okay, the first week, three games has to be three wins,' and we did that. So now we're looking forward to Arsenal.

"I can't see the future, but we try to improve to not concede three goals, but we know we are very dangerous up front, that we will score goals.

"I think against Arsenal is a good test, but I think it was against Fulham and Brighton as well. They are both great teams and we won those games, so we are looking forward to the next one now."

It won't define Chelsea's season if they lose. But if they win, the belief of the squad will exponentially grow, knowing they've managed to overcome a huge hurdle so early into the season.

title: Yen's changing fortunes might finally be spooking the bears
description: , Rae Wee and Atsuko Aoyama LONDON/SINGAPORE/TOKYO, Sept 4 (Reuters) - Six weeks after hitting a four-decade low against the dollar, the tide appears to be turning for the battered
fullText:
LONDON/SINGAPORE/TOKYO, Sept 4 (Reuters) - Six weeks after hitting a four-decade low against the dollar, the tide appears to be turning for the battered yen as a host of factors finally smoke out traders who have spent years betting against the Japanese currency.

While central bank rate hikes and record currency intervention have failed to provide lasting support for the ‌yen, new tailwinds from capital repatriation, unwinding carry trades and U.S. political pressure are now giving short speculators cause to rethink their long-term game.

The yen is on track for a roughly 2% surge against ‌the greenback this week — the most since a rare joint U.S. and Japan intervention at the end of July to lift the yen.

"The market psychology around the yen appears to be changing," said Rong Ren Goh, a fixed income portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments. "Investors seem increasingly reluctant to ​aggressively short the JPY (yen), particularly with the prospect of a BOJ rate hike in September adding another layer of risk to the trade."

The Bank of Japan is expected to lift its key rate by 25 basis points (bps) this month and markets are also contemplating the possibility of a 50-bps hike or a series of rapid increases in coming months.

Nevertheless, a 50-bps September hike is still seen as extremely unlikely, particularly under Governor Kazuo Ueda's cautious leadership.

All the same, the shift in mood is backed up by money flows. Data from Citigroup indicate positioning on the yen has flipped from bearish to bullish since the start of August, with interbank flow data showing leveraged funds, banks and real-money investors all net-buying yen this week.

The convergence ‌of central bank policy, investment flows and speculative positioning is adding to volatility. The ⁠yen is also up almost 2% against the euro and Australian dollar this week.

Stephen Jen, CEO and co-CIO of Eurizon SLJ Asset Management, said the risk of a rapid unwind of yen-based carry trades is rising, in a similar way to 1998 when the collapse of Long-Term Capital Management forced banks and hedge funds to rapidly deleverage.

The yen has long ⁠been the favoured currency for the carry trade, where investors borrow cheaply in yen to invest elsewhere.

"When a currency is so extremely undervalued, and positioning is so extended, movements like this one will occur increasingly frequently before a big move," Jen said. "It's a bit like earthquakes. The tectonic plates are grating on each other with great forces."

title: Has there been a changing of guard for London sides in the WSL?
description: With the Women's Super League season starting up, are Arsenal in a better position than Chelsea to challenge for the title?
fullText:
Last season, Arsenal finished above Chelsea in the Women's Super League for the first time in seven years.

The last occasion was in 2018-19, the most recent title for the Gunners.

In between, Chelsea finished top of the pile for six straight seasons.

In 2025-26, while both trailed in the wake of eventual champions Manchester City, Arsenal leapfrogged their London rivals to finish second.

They also knocked the Blues out of the Women's Champions League in the quarter-finals.

So did those results signal a changing of the guard in the capital?

And what about London City Lionesses, who opened the WSL season with victory over Manchester United on Friday and now boast Spain superstar Alexia Putellas in their ranks?

This summer, both Arsenal and Chelsea have experienced turnover in their squads.

The Gunners lost stalwarts Beth Mead and Katie McCabe among others but have freshened their team with England midfielder Georgia Stanway, Spain World Cup winner Ona Batlle and Switzerland captain Geraldine Reuteler among a glut of exciting signings.

At Stamford Bridge, Chelsea snapped up McCabe on a free transfer and splashed cash on Manchester United's Melvine Malard but can no longer call on Sam Kerr and Millie Bright, two defining players from their era of dominance.

With their latest quest for silverware getting started this weekend, it was Arsenal boss Renee Slegers who struck a more confident tone about her expectations for the season.

"We've been open about it - the WSL title is something we're going after," said Slegers, before her side open the season at Brighton on Sunday. "It's something where we really have our mind set.

"Of course there's a big belief in what we are doing, the quality that we possess and the different tools we have to use. There's a real hunger."

Sunday's game offers Arsenal an early return to Broadfield Stadium in Crawley, where their bid to chase down Manchester City last season was ended by a 1-1 draw against Brighton in May.

A number of similar results cost Arsenal, particularly at the beginning of the year, and Slegers is determined to avoid lightning striking twice.

"We've spoken about it with the staff, the captains, the player group," she said. "Everyone is aware of it. We know the hurdles we had last year - and that's what we're working towards.

"The quality of players that we have here, there's so many things that we can bring to a game now. I'm really happy about it."

And is this her strongest squad at Arsenal?

At Chelsea, manager Sonia Bompastor was less bullish about her side's chances of regaining the WSL title.

"I'm trying to be as honest as possible. Chelsea is in a transitional phase," Bompastor said. "We are rebuilding, regenerating the squad.

"As much as I know my job is to win many games and to win trophies and I'm desperate for that - but it also takes time for the squad to gel together."

"The DNA for Chelsea is to win and we want to make sure we go as far as possible in every competition."

Saturday, 5 September, 12:30 BST

Chelsea open the season against Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime, live on BBC One, and have been installed as favourites by Opta's supercomputer, which gives the Blues a 39.9% chance, external of winning the league.

Not that Bompastor is paying any attention.

"I remember sitting here last season and someone told me the same," she said. "Our percentage was higher than this season! I'm not too focused on what numbers and what is coming from AI or computers."

She believes that this season will be the toughest yet and, while acknowledging the significant threat from champions Manchester City, she says challengers will come from all directions.

"The beauty in this league is that many clubs are in a position to win the title," Bompastor said. "It was already the most competitive league in the world and it's becoming stronger every season.

"Every game is so difficult but that's good. I'm excited for it."

One of those could be London City, who after finishing sixth in their maiden WSL season have spent big this summer.

Their goal is likely to be challenging the established elite in the WSL, although ambitious owner Michelle Kang will not settle for that.

She has previously told BBC Sport that London City "have an aspiration to be at the top of the game" and starting the season with a convincing performance against Manchester United lends credence to that plan.

title: How London City proved they can live up to the hype
description: There was an expectation on London City Lionesses to live up to the hype and deliver in the Women's Super League's season opener - and they did.
fullText:
There was an expectation on London City Lionesses to live up to the hype and deliver in the Women's Super League's season opener - and they did.

Eder Maestre's side showed they are not just a starting XI of superstars but a team who may gel quicker than many expected.

They came away from Hayes Lane, in front of a full crowd of 5,402 home fans, with an impressive 2-1 victory over Manchester United.

The scoreline could have been worse for United as London City dominated the first half and showed flashes of individual brilliance, amid a clear structure and intent.

Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas made her debut and was the glue in midfield while others stole the limelight.

US billionaire owner Michele Kang was also present, donning a new match shirt with her name on the back and posing for photos with fans before kick-off.

"It was really fun to win today," said Delphine Cascarino, one of many international stars in the London City squad.

"I think we have a chance to do something this season. We are trying to build something huge and achieve big things and I think we have a chance."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

The tone was set in the first minute by London City, immediately showing their intent with a strike from Alanna Kennedy in the first minute that won a corner.

They allowed United no time to settle, pressing from the front and taking advantage of the visitors' hesitancy in possession.

A flick from Putellas here and there, tenacity from Kennedy and quick feet from Grace Geyoro were all frequently on show.

But it was the fluidity of London City's link-up play that caught the eye - a group of superstars looking like a good team in the first game of the season.

Surely it pleased manager Maestre?

"Yeah, I think we were really strong, mostly in the first half," said Maestre.

"We are facing Manchester United. You can't imagine you will be dominant for the whole game because they have a lot of good players.

"The team showed how capable we are and what we were trying to create so I'm very proud."

London City were a bit of an unknown entity in pre-season given the arrival of several big-name players.

Ex-United and England goalkeeper Mary Earps started on the bench alongside fellow new arrival Nicole Anyomi but Spain's Mapi Leon and forward Rosa Kafaji started.

Danielle van de Donk, who spent most of last season injured, starred and scored, while Kennedy's header brought the opener when it deflected off Julia Zigiotti.

Putting the pieces together is the challenge with which Maestre has been tasked but Friday night was a fine start.

"It's one of the most challenging situations for coaches when you have many talented players but you are trying to align everyone on the same page and achieve something big," said Maestre.

"We need very good positional game and that flexibility to feel strong in a match. That is why I'm really happy with the performance.

"To have all the players on the same page and establish that relationship is really good."

In contrast, opponents Manchester United - one of those London City hope to overtake this season - clearly need more time to adapt to new manager Eva Olid's ways.

When she addressed the media for the first time on Thursday, the Spaniard promised brave, attacking football and a desire to dominate possession.

But what transpired in a painful opening 45 minutes for United supporters was a team short on confidence and lacking threat, failing to produce a shot of any kind.

The second half saw improvement but it came too late.

Indeed, United did not have a shot on target until the ninth minute of second-half stoppage time, substitute Simi Awujo's goal giving the scoreline a friendlier look.

"I always say it's a process. In three weeks, I don't think we can believe we are a team that will dominate the ball and attack," said ex-Hearts boss Olid, who was appointed on 5 August.

"Of course, I think it's more something mental. In the first half, I didn't feel like the players were believing. At half time I said: 'Listen, this is not us.'

"In the first half, we were forcing things, the basics in possession were wrong and we were giving them the ball to attack. That is not what we want to be.

"In the second half, we were building through the middle, playing in the pockets and moving through the lines. That is us. That felt like my team in the second half."

Olid said it was her job to help her players believe they can be better and was defiant when asked if United could compete with the quality displayed by London City.

She said the difference between the two teams on the day was down to confidence.

"If we play as we did in the second half, I don't think the gap is that big," she added.

"I think the structure was wrong in attack - when the structure isn't right, the players are lost. We fixed that but mentally, the players were not believing.

"London City pressed well and took our mistakes to create chances. They did very well in the first half but in the second half, I felt we were in the match."

fullText:
US tech company has sued London mayor after he prevented it from working with Metropolitan police

Sadiq Khan has agreed for his text messages and emails to be searched as part of a legal battle with Palantir, the high court has been told, after he prevented the US technology company from working with the Metropolitan police.

The London mayor stepped in to block a £50m deal between Palantir and the Met in May, with the artificial intelligence developer suing Khan’s office over the decision.

Legal representatives for the mayor said they “did not originally consider it necessary” for Khan to be among those to have their communications searched before next year’s court case. But they relented, citing persistence from Palantir.

Sarah Brown, Khan’s former director of communications, who now works for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, will also have her correspondence searched.

The proposed two-year deal would have allowed Palantir, which works for the Israeli military and the Trump administration in its immigration crackdown, to provide AI technology to automate intelligence analysis in criminal investigations.

But the Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime (Mopac), which oversees large Scotland Yard contracts, said there had been a “clear and serious breach” of procurement rules. It said police had seriously considered only one supplier (Palantir).

After the announcement, Palantir accused Khan of “putting politics above public safety” before declaring in June that it planned to sue the London mayor.

At a preliminary hearing on Thursday, the high court was told Khan and more than a dozen other Mopac and Greater London Authority officials would be classed as “custodians”.

The designation means their digital communications, including text messages, WhatsApp messages, and Microsoft Teams chats – insofar as they exist – will be searched for anything relevant to the issues in the legal tussle. These will then be disclosed to Palantir.

Joseph Barrett KC, for the mayor’s office, said in written submissions: “Mopac did not originally consider it necessary or proportionate for the mayor to be added as a custodian, given that the decision was taken by the deputy mayor for policing and crime; his senior position; and the likelihood that any documents held by him would be held by other individuals.

“However, Palantir has persisted in its requests, and Mopac has consented on a pragmatic basis.”

Brown, who in July moved from the mayor’s office to be appointed director of communications at Downing Street, was also listed as a custodian, meaning she too will have her correspondence searched, the court heard.

The decision to include Brown comes after Palantir said in court documents outlining its claim that press articles regarding the mayor’s office vetoing the Met deal cited concerns about Palantir’s values and ethics. Mopac has confirmed Brown “initiated” press briefings about the move.

The date range for the communication searches is still to be determined.

 Mopac reportedly is demanding to see Palantir’s own internal documents related to the deal, which the company is said to be resisting.

title: We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor
description: London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.
fullText:
London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.

BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.

However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.

"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.

Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.

A late-night fight in London - potentially in the early hours - could mean it draws a larger television audience in the US.

Brent Council, the local authority involved in any approval, has said a potential extension of the curfew would need to be assessed by Wembley's safety advisory group.

It remains unclear how late that curfew could be pushed back.

"Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are two great British boxers. Both have been world champions," Khan said.

"They both recognise and love the fans in this country who have supported them throughout their careers, amateur and professional.

"Wembley has hosted many fantastic events, including bouts involving Tyson and Anthony. We, the fans, want to see them box live in London."

There is hope that the venue will be finalised in the coming days. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said he wants an announcement this week, with a news conference to follow next week.

BBC Sport has contacted Sela for comment.

Fury calls Joshua a 'coward' as wait for announcement continues

Hearn says his side signed a contract for the bout to take place in the United Kingdom, while Sela and Netflix's preference would be the United States, to cater for American audiences.

Matchroom Boxing's Hearn has previously said Joshua's contract specifically stipulated a UK venue and would need to be renegotiated for the fight to take place Stateside.

Hearn says he has since set out terms under which Matchroom would agree to the change, with negotiations continuing over a possible move to New York.

The contact from Sela represents a significant development from the end of July, when sources close to the mayor told BBC Sport there had been no approach from the fight's organisers.

But the lack of progress since that initial contact underlines the uncertainty still surrounding Wembley's chances of hosting the contest.

"I'm hoping the promoters understand that not only will you get 100,000 people watching this bout live, you'll get millions watching it across the globe, where both boxers are cheered on by their loyal fans," Khan said.

fullText:
London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang says her club's new shirt sponsorship deal with sports brand Nike is the largest in the women's game - and worth more than those of some Premier League sides.

The current largest deal for a women's side is believed to be for the new National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) franchise in Atlanta, which is set to join the competition in 2028.

Atlanta's shirt deal is reportedly worth about $4m (£2.96m), a similar figure to that of new entrants to the Premier League and more than most Championship clubs.

"I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal," Kang told BBC Sport. "It is higher than the Atlanta number.

"I can absolutely also share that it is higher than some of the men's Premier League front-of-shirt deals. It's huge. That's why it's landmark."

The news comes after a big summer for London City which has seen them sign two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and Spain defender Mapi Leon from Barcelona, as well as ex-England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Lyon winger Kadidiatou Diani.

Unmasking London City's Spanish superstar

Media Day Diaries: Inside London City Lionesses

Kang added: "There are so many other people who believe in the future of women's football. They didn't make this decision lightly - they did not write a charity cheque. They believe in the future and they believe together we will invest and build this future together."

All Women's Super League clubs apart from London City share shirt sponsors with their men's teams.

London City's record is only for independent women's clubs, of which they are the only one in England's top flight.

title: Netherlands moves billions in gold to London in 'crisis preparedness' move
description: The Dutch central bank removes some of its gold reserves from the US and Canada, saying it is because of "increasing geopolitical unrest".
fullText:
The Dutch central bank (DNB) has confirmed that billions of dollars in gold has been taken out of north America and relocated to London, citing "increasing geopolitical unrest".

DNB said on Wednesday that 86 tonnes of gold had been removed from the US and Canada in a complex operation that took several months. It is now being held by the Bank of England, where the precious metal can be traded more easily "in a crisis situation".

Bank president Olaf Sleijpen said the move was "necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness".

The decision comes amid an ongoing trade dispute between the US and Canada, with both countries announcing fresh tariffs on each other after failed trade talks.

DNB said the transfer, which took place between March and August, saw 27 tonnes of gold bars moved from New York and Ottawa to Zeist in the Netherlands.

A similar quantity and quality was then moved to London, with no need to melt the bars down.

Exactly how so much gold was transported across the Atlantic Ocean has not been revealed.

The rest of the transfer was carried out by selling the gold in New York, and repurchasing it in London, the bank said.

"Combining the processes of buying and selling and physical transport has allowed DNB to spread the risks associated with such a complex physical gold relocation," the statement said.

DNB did not confirm what it was referring to with its mention of "geopolitical unrest" but the US economy remains in an uncertain position due to the country's ongoing war with Iran, which has impacted global trade.

Canada, meanwhile, has been hit hard by US tariffs on its key sectors of steel, aluminium, lumber and automobiles as well as an additional 50% levy on about C$28bn ($20bn; £15bn) of Canadian goods announced in August.

DNB said that gold that is held with the Bank of England "is regarded as the world's most easily tradable gold," and therefore more readily available in a crisis than if it was still in the US or Canada.

Prior to Wednesday's announcement, the DNB held 31.3% of its gold in New York and 19.7% in Ottawa. This has now fallen to 18.5% in both countries.

The total Dutch gold stock was 612.4 tonnes at the end of 2025 and has been valued at €72.2 billion, DNB said.

The bank's share of gold in London has increased from 18.1% to 32.1% after the move, while it still holds 30.8% of its reserves in the Netherlands.

fullText:
Wayve robotaxis added to Uber app and will have human in front ready to take over if needed – but only 15 cars licensed

Londoners are now able to hire self-driving taxis for the first time, after rides in Wayve’s autonomous vehicles were added to the Uber app on Thursday.

The chances of landing a robotaxi on request immediately are slim, with only 15 vehicles so far licensed. That contrasts with the more than 100,000 private hire vehicles in the capital – roughly the same number of Uber customers who have registered to take autonomous rides.

The cars will still come with a licensed human driver sitting in the front seat, ready to take over the controls should the need arise.

Transport for London last month licensed Uber and the UK tech company Wayve’s modified Ford Mustang cars as private hire vehicles, whose conditions still require a safety driver supervising.

Regulatory approval for vehicles in fully autonomous operations without a safety driver needs to be granted under a separate government process and agency, the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency, and is now seen as unlikely this year.

Nonetheless, Thursday’s launch marks a significant milestone and has allowed Uber to steal a march in the race by tech companies to bring driverless taxis into London, seen as a crucial market for a wider European rollout. Google-owned Waymo and the Chinese company Baidu are testing their robotaxis in the UK capital.

Alex Kendall, the chief executive and co-founder of Wayve, said he was proud to introduce the company’s AI Driver technology to the public for the first time in London, “our home city and one of the most complex driving environments in the world”.

Kendall said the technology was “still maturing” but robotaxi services without a safety driver would come, although he declined to predict exactly when: “I don’t want to put a timeline on it, but we’re pushing as fast as we can.”

He said Wayve would be moving to “scalable manufacturer-produced vehicles” – new Nissan Leaf robotaxis with its technology – and needs to “validate the safety metrics on that platform”, as well as secure regulatory approval.

“We’re working on all three in parallel. As soon as they come together, we’ll launch [fully] driverless services,” Kendall said.

Wayve’s self-driving technology is based on an AI learning model rather than the mapping used by rivals such as Waymo.

On a brief autonomous test drive with the Guardian in Westminster this week, all passed smoothly, with Kendall notably pleased by the car deciding to pull away again and re-park after stopping in front of gates that other cars were attempting to pass through. “That was quite human-like – really cool,” he said. “We’ve done a lot work to make sure the car can park in appropriate spots that are socially acceptable.”

The cars will be hailed and unlocked through the Uber app. The driver will introduce themselves with an appropriately robotic script, explaining that they will no longer speak during the ride but can be requested to take over control of the vehicle if the customer prefers.

While they will be the first self-driving cabs for hire in London, fully driverless services are in operation in many cities worldwide, primarily in the US and China, as well as the United Arab Emirates.

Uber partnered in launching Europe’s first commercial robotaxi service earlier this summer in Zagreb, Croatia, with a human driver onboard as in London.

Sarfraz Maredia, the head of autonomous mobility at Uber, said the London launch was “a major milestone in scaling safe, accessible AV technology in a city with some of the world’s most complex roads”.

He said: “The benefit for consumers should be, over time, that it’s both safer and cheaper. Today, nobody’s able to operate AVs cheaper than a traditional human-driven ride, so that’s going to take a while to prove.”

Maredia said Uber had heard concerns from drivers but said he believed they would not be put out of work: “One of the most common ones we hear from our drivers is: ‘Hey, I drive in this city and it’s very complex, and I don’t think this product is going to be able to compete with me anytime soon.’”

He added: “We always want Uber to be a platform where both human drivers and AVs can operate, and because the market and our business are still growing here we think that’s going to be true for a long time.”

Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, said: “This is a major milestone for the future of transport in London, as British innovation brings this technology on to our roads and gives passengers more choice.

“Today’s announcement further cements Wayve’s status as a technology trailblazer here in the UK, and highlights how British innovation is helping drive investment and growth in transport.”

David McMullen, a senior organiser at the GMB union, said: “With hundreds of thousands of people employed to drive every day, we need to be really careful with the rollout of driverless cars unless we are prepared to see unprecedented levels of social and economic disruption.”

title: Exclusive-Banks rush to swap higher-risk credit assets for Bank of England cash
description: , Lawrence White and David Milliken LONDON, Sept 2 (Reuters) - British banks are increasingly pledging higher-risk assets such as loans linked to high-interest store cards and vehicle
fullText:
LONDON, Sept 2 (Reuters) - British banks are increasingly pledging higher-risk assets such as loans linked to high-interest store cards and vehicle leases as collateral at the Bank of England, a Reuters review of BoE filings shows.

On August 18, banks pledged £1.9 billion ($2.6 billion) worth of the BoE's highest-risk type of collateral ‌at its weekly auction for six-month funds, its data shows, the most since March 2020 and three times as much as in the previous week.

In total, Reuters calculations show the BoE ‌has about £17.8 billion of what it calls "Level C" collateral on its books from its Indexed Long-Term Repo (ILTR), up from £8.7 billion a year ago and under £1 billion in mid-2024.

Such transactions show the extent to which Britain's central bank is exposed to higher-risk and ​potentially illiquid assets. The European Central Bank, meanwhile, has tightened its criteria for acceptable collateral in recent years, worried that a central bank stamp of approval increases demand for riskier securities that could be hard to sell in a crisis.

A BoE spokesperson said the ILTR was designed to allow firms to use a broad range of assets as collateral while allowing the BoE to protect itself through what it described as robust risk management.

"Our facilities are open for business and we welcome their increased use," the spokesperson said.

British commercial banks use cash held in accounts at the BoE for wholesale transactions. The growing use of the ILTR to receive this ‌cash is an intended consequence of the BoE's 2022 decision to reverse ⁠the £895 billion of quantitative easing it undertook from 2009 to 2021, which flooded the financial system with cash.

The securitisation of mortgage-backed debt and other loans was a major contributor to the 2008 financial crisis as it encouraged risk-taking by lenders who were able to quickly sell the debt on.

"The BoE has got good reasons for wanting to buy grade C assets but there's a risk that if they do too much then that can encourage bad lending. I think they probably ​understand ​that already," said William Allen, a visiting fellow at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research and a former ​head of the BoE's money markets division.

fullText:
SINGAPORE/LONDON/NEW YORK, Sept 2 (Reuters) - Bond prices continued to slide in Asia and Europe on Wednesday, pushing borrowing costs to multi-decade highs as the Middle East conflict drives up energy prices and layers concerns about inflation on top of worries about ballooning government debt.

Sovereign bond yields are a reference point for asset prices across financial markets and the higher price of ‌money means elevated mortgage rates for consumers and tough choices for government spending as funding costs climb.

Japan's 10-year yield was perched above 3% for the first time in 30 years, while rising gas prices meant German ‌10-year Bund yields were stuck at their highest since 2011 and Britain's equivalent was at its highest since 2008. Yields rise as prices fall and vice versa.

A confluence of factors was at play, said State Street's head of macro strategy, Michael Metcalfe, with rising energy prices causing traders to bet ​on rate hikes, pushing up short-dated yields.

"The narrative is also getting wrapped up with longer-term concerns about the fiscal path. In France and the UK, we are going to get news on budgets soon. So, there are not many positives out there," Metcalfe said.

Bond sales from big tech companies aggressively raising money to fund the AI boom have added pressure on the sovereign bond market, as deep-pocketed U.S. tech firms compete with governments for investors' capital.

Naka Matsuzawa, chief macro strategist at Nomura Securities in Tokyo, said so-called hyperscalers' willingness to pay reasonably high rates was pulling up yields broadly, with the focus now on whether growth can rise along with them to help economies cope with the higher rates.

Yields can continue to rise as investors demand a higher premium, said ‌Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.

title: Fake 10 Downing Street listing on Booking.com highlights security failures
description: Consumer watchdog Which? set up and accepted payment for fake listing for ‘1 bed apartment in heart of London’
fullText:
Consumer watchdog Which? set up and accepted payment for fake listing for ‘1 bed apartment in heart of London’

Successive politicians have clawed their way past colleagues over the years to call the residence home. Yet in an offer that probably seemed too good to be true, the property site Booking.com has been accused of “systemic security failures” after it was able to set up and accept payment for a fake listing for 10 Downing Street.

A property listed as a “1 bedroom apartment in the heart of London” – with the exact address and a picture of the prime minister’s home – was listed on 18 June by researchers from the consumer watchdog Which?.

The listing, which promised a four-minute walk to the Houses of Parliament, was set up so that users had to request a stay and were unable to reserve and pay automatically.

The booking window opened briefly and closed so that a test could be carried out by a researcher from Which?. The consumer watchdog said a payment for a week-long stay had been processed by the digital travel site that enables users to book hotels and other accommodation as well as flights and car rentals.

The money had still not been refunded more than six weeks after it had been set up, according to Which?, which is associated with the Consumers Association charity.

A fake review was also uploaded to the site, describing the stay as “exceptional” and enjoying the experience of “hanging out with Larry the cat”, in a reference to Downing Street’s resident feline.

Despite Booking.com sending a message saying the review would be checked by a team of moderators, the consumer watchdog said it had been added almost immediately.

The team of researchers were also said to have used Booking.com’s mailing system to send an external URL asking the representative for credit card details to confirm the booking, Which? said.

The watchdog claimed the travel site had told them it had the ability to block URLs being sent through the messaging system if it suspected fraudulent activity, but it had not done so.

The listing was finally removed on 27 August, six weeks after it went live.

Rory Boland, the editor of Which? Travel, said: “If Booking.com’s so-called sophisticated AI systems can’t spot that 10 Downing Street is not a holiday rental, then it’s no wonder scammers can exploit the platform so easily.”

The watchdog said its investigation had “uncovered systemic security failures across the platform” and urged Ofcom, the UK’s communications regulator, to investigate.

A Booking.com spokesperson said: “This limited test is not a true reflection of the experience of millions of listings on our platform. The property added by Which? was not visible to customers or ‘live’ for the time period referenced.

“We use a range of checks, verification measures and artificial intelligence, which help us detect and remove the majority of fraudulent listings within 24 hours.”

It said that as the property was not open and bookable, some of its automatic fraud controls were not triggered to completely remove the fraud listing.

An Ofcom spokesperson said platforms have legal duties obliging them to take down illegal content generated by users once it is known. “Booking.com is not in scope of future rules that will apply to paid-for fraudulent advertising, and any change to that would be a matter for government,” they said.

title: Blockade succeeds where sanctions failed as Iran oil exports stall
description: , Enes Tunagur and Robert Harvey LONDON, Sept 1 (Reuters) - For the first time on record, Iran has gone about seven weeks without shipping meaningful crude exports through the Strait
fullText:
LONDON, Sept 1 (Reuters) - For the first time on record, Iran has gone about seven weeks without shipping meaningful crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, as a U.S. naval blockade succeeds where years of sanctions ‌failed by cutting off one of Tehran's main sources of foreign-currency earnings.

Unlike previous sanctions campaigns, when Iranian crude continued reaching buyers despite restrictions, ‌the current blockade has stopped fresh crude cargoes reaching China, Tehran's only major remaining oil customer, increasing pressure on government finances and foreign-currency reserves.

Since the U.S. reinstated its blockade on Iran on ​July 14 as part of their six-month conflict, no Iranian crude cargoes have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz to China, according to Kpler, Vortexa and TankerTrackers.com.

As a result, Iran can only sell crude to China from floating storage in Asia, which it cannot replenish as crude accumulates aboard tankers inside the strait.

"Even at the height of maximum-pressure sanctions in 2019-20, some Iranian crude cleared Hormuz every single month; at no point did outbound flows fall to near-zero for a sustained stretch ‌as they have since mid-July," Vortexa analyst Claire Jungman ⁠said.

Iran loaded about 220,000 to 255,000 barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in August, according to Vortexa and Kpler estimates, down from roughly 740,000 bpd in July and about 2 million bpd in March.

The collapse in exports is draining ⁠one of Iran's main sources of foreign-currency income and could force Tehran to finance spending by printing money, risking even higher inflation, Kpler analyst Homayoun Falakshahi said.

The International Monetary Fund estimates Iran's inflation rate at nearly 70% this year, the world's third-highest after Venezuela and Sudan.

Last week, Washington sought to increase the pressure by threatening countries that ​continue ​trading with Tehran, while stopping short of immediately imposing penalties.

fullText:
Amelia Dimoldenberg says publicists ignored her interview show for years but she can now be picky over A-list guests

Just a decade ago, Amelia Dimoldenberg found it impossible to drum up any mainstream celebrities to come on her mock date YouTube show, in which she chats awkwardly with guests over chicken and chips.

Even persuading a local actor connected with her London youth club to come on took years of prodding. Managers of A-listers with movies or albums to push instead battled to claim a spot on the hallowed cushions of the primetime TV chatshow sofa.

Yet after those early years of rejection, Dimoldenberg has said that she has reached a watershed moment. Such is the influence of her Chicken Shop Date show, she says it now ranks alongside Graham Norton’s chatshow or BBC Radio 1 for celebrities seeking media cut-through.

“When I started the show in 2014, no publicist and no manager would let their talent come on a YouTube show – that was just insane,” she told the Edinburgh TV festival. “I would be banging down the doors, it was just so challenging. Now it’s so fascinating because it’s the opposite.

“If your publicist is coming to you and you’ve got a movie out, or you’ve got an album rollout campaign, now I do think one of the first things up there on the list of things to do would be to come on Chicken Shop Date.

“That has always been the ambition – my ambition – to make it as important as going on Graham Norton or going on Greg James, Radio 1, for example. So I’ve achieved that goal.”

Dimoldenberg’s rise is a prime example of how digital platforms have radically reshaped the media world, with viewers across all ages switching to YouTube, especially under-35s.

Dimoldenberg has shared the ketchup with Ed Sheeran, Charli xcx and Jennifer Lawrence, although Lawrence got Dimoldenberg’s name wrong. Even Paul McCartney turned up for a date in a vegan chicken shop this year, declining Dimoldenberg’s suggestion that he adopt a pet otter.

Dimoldenberg initially focused on interviewing figures from the UK rap and grime scene when she launched Chicken Shop Date in 2014. She secured her first big name, the actor Daniel Kaluuya, because he was a fan of the show.

Her interviews have repeatedly gone viral since then, thanks to Louis Theroux rapping or the chemistry between Dimoldenberg and the actor Andrew Garfield. “I didn’t realise fully how much the audience would catch on to how obsessed he is with me,” she said.

She is increasingly picky over guests and rejects anyone who wants to be on the show only as part of a “press run” publicising their latest project.

It marks a shift in the media hierarchy and underlines YouTube’s muscle. The platform’s rise has become so all-consuming in the TV world that Pedro Pina, YouTube’s head for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, was invited to give the keynote MacTaggart lecture at the Edinburgh TV festival last week, the industry’s most important get-together of the year.

Pina used the speech to insist YouTube was “not the villain” about to destroy the TV industry, though he made clear the age of monopoly for TV networks was over.

Sure enough, the temptation of having total creative control – as well as scooping up the ads, sponsors and brand deals that can follow – is now enticing more established media names to try their luck on YouTube.

The presenter Holly Willoughby launched her YouTube channel over the summer, amassing 22,000 subscribers so far. Amol Rajan will finish as a presenter of BBC Radio 4’s Today programme this week and launch a YouTube show, The Amol Rajan Connection. The road from TV personality to YouTuber is already well established in the US.

Yet in a media world that continues to converge, Dimoldenberg is moving in the other direction, seeking success in conventional movies and television. She is writing a teen drama for the BBC, similar to the show Skins, which ran for seven series on E4.

She is also writing a Hollywood romcom, in which she will star as a journalist who finds romance with a celebrity after interviewing them. Other than the chicken, it is a plot that sounds close to home.

“It’s a character that I’ve been playing half my life, so I feel like I know it very well,” she said. “It’s definitely just an exaggeration of who I am.”

description: Daniel Dubois will defend his WBO heavyweight world title against the man he dethroned Fabio Wardley in a rematch on 17 October in London.
fullText:
Daniel Dubois will defend his WBO heavyweight world title against former champion Fabio Wardley in a highly anticipated rematch on 17 October at London's O2 Arena.

Londoner Dubois, 28, dethroned Wardley with an 11th-round stoppage in a thrilling all-British showdown in Manchester in May to become a two-time world champion.

It was announced during Saturday's undercard of Moses Itauma's IBF heavyweight world title fight with Filip Hrgovic, with Dubois and Wardley facing off in the ring.

Dubois said he is predicting a "dominant victory" before adding: "Let's get it on. It's just a war.

"When you get in the water, you're going to get wet. We will see. Give me some of that face-to-face - boy."

The first meeting lived up to its billing, with two of the division's biggest punchers producing a dramatic fight that showcased the power of both men.

Wardley dropped Dubois twice early in the contest, but a bloodied Wardley absorbed heavy punishment before the referee stopped the bout.

It was the first defeat of the 31-year-old's professional career in his 22nd bout.

"It didn't take long at all [to agree]. The O2 is like a home away from home for me," Fabio Wardley said on DAZN.

"Looking forward to getting straight back into it. Going to be a rematch and going to be revenge.

"We came into the fight with all the confidence in the world, but adjustments needed to be made."

The Ipswich fighter's rise through the sport has been remarkable. Having only taken up boxing at the age of 19, he progressed through the unlicensed white-collar scene before reaching the top of the heavyweight division.

Dubois, meanwhile, has experienced the full spectrum of boxing's highs and lows.

The 26-fight veteran has suffered three defeats during his career but rebuilt himself to claim world honours twice, with his victory over Wardley marking the latest chapter in his comeback story.

The winner of the rematch could be in line for a blockbuster fight next summer against fellow Briton Itauma, provided the heavyweight prospect secures a world title of his own.

The winner of the contest between Itauma and Hrgovic will be required to face mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez.

Should Itauma - who is aiming to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion in history after Mike Tyson - come through both fights, promoter Frank Warren has suggested a potential Wembley Stadium clash with the winner of Dubois-Wardley II next summer.

The heavyweight division remains fragmented following Oleksandr Usyk's decision to vacate his titles. Russian Murat Gassiev currently holds the WBA belt, while Germany's Agit Kabayel is the WBC champion.

title: Newcastle show there's plenty of life after Tonali
description: Newcastle United sold Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur, but the club look to have reinvested the money wisely following United's 2-0 win in north London.
fullText:
Sandro Tonali anticipated being "more nervous" than usual about coming up against former club Newcastle United for the first time.

You suspect the Tottenham Hotspur midfielder felt a little sick following their 2-0 defeat on Saturday evening.

"Sandro, what's the score?" the away fans taunted in the closing stages as the substituted Italian looked on.

This bruising loss was certainly not the reunion Tonali had in mind after joining Spurs for a fee worth up to £100m last month.

It is still very early days, of course, but Newcastle appear to have reinvested the money wisely after spending a similar combined amount on midfielder Nico Gonzalez, defender Amar Dedic and goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

A number of the players head coach Matthias Jaissle inherited, such as goalscorers Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa, also look reborn.

Yet he was rightly not getting carried away following his first Premier League win.

"We have our own goals and we are clear with that," Jaissle said. "We are also realistic. Now you write everything is top, everything is great.

"We don't follow that too much. We are emotionally very stable and don't see the highs higher than it is now.

"It is a moment to enjoy as well after that start, but we are also smart enough to see a long journey ahead of us and there will be challenges as well."

Jaissle, by his own admission, "likes challenges" and this was certainly a big one to take on.

It is exactly 30 days since predecessor Eddie Howe oversaw what proved to be his final match in charge, a sobering 4-1 friendly defeat against Bristol City, before stepping down.

Newcastle had sold Tonali. Anthony Gordon had left for Barcelona. Captain Bruno Guimaraes' sights were set on a move to Arsenal.

The start of the season was also rapidly approaching.

Newcastle have made further additions since then, but only one of their seven summer signings, Gonzalez, has previously played in the Premier League.

All of the new arrivals are aged 24 and under.

Yet you would not necessarily know it by the immediate impact full-back Dedic has made following his £30m move from Benfica, or how Hornicek has stood up to the physicality of the Premier League since his £25.7m switch from Braga.

It could easily be forgotten, given what happened after the break at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, but Hornicek was among those to play an important role in this win after making three saves at crucial moments in the first half.

No wonder Jaissle clenched his fists on the touchline after Hornicek got a strong hand behind Jan Paul van Hecke's header.

There was a similarly enthusiastic reaction from the former Hoffenheim defender when Lewis Hall blocked a goalbound effort from Pedro Porro in the first half.

"In the first half, we didn't play a really good game, but we could really count on everyone throwing everything into every ball and every cross," Jaissle said.

"This is the commitment and belief that we can keep the clean sheet, so that makes me proud."

Although Newcastle defeated Spurs last season, too, there were also a number of games when the visitors wilted in such circumstances.

Newcastle won just four of their 19 top-flight matches on the road and, home or away, they had not previously kept a single clean sheet since March.

However, going in level in their first away day of this campaign gave Newcastle the chance to regroup at half-time.

The visitors sought to be more aggressive after the break and clinically took Spurs apart with their only two shots on target.

For the first, just as he did in the opening stages, new signing Gonzalez hit a stunning cross field ball over the head of Spurs left-back Andy Robertson for the advancing Dedic to flick on to Elanga, who turned Tonali inside the box and fired the ball in off the post.

"It is something that I spoke about with the coach, even before the game," Gonzalez said.

"He wanted me to see these kind of balls and I tried a few in the first half and the second half, and we scored.

"In the second half we said, 'we have to keep doing this' because it is really hard to defend players like Amar, a full-back that comes this fast from behind. Normally wingers don't defend these kind of balls very well.

"It's something that we have to keep doing and I hope it gives us many more goals this season."

For Newcastle's second, Sean Steur's corner was headed down by fellow substitute Nick Woltemade and Wissa improvised with a clever overhead kick to double his side's lead.

For all the focus on Newcastle's new arrivals, it was rather fitting that two players who endured difficult first seasons at the club stepped up under Jaissle once again as Elanga and Wissa built on improved showings against Liverpool on the opening weekend.

"He's a really dynamic manager so we need to give everything," Wissa told Sky Sports. "I think he's the best signing."

title: Itauma punches himself out against Hrgovic in world-title fight
description: Filip Hrgovic shatters Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appears to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight world-title contest in London.
fullText:
Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.

Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.

Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.

Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar.

"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind," Hrgovic said.

"From the first round, I saw his gassing out. He started fast. I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came I needed to push. That is what I did."

With the vacant IBF title on the line, victory would have made Itauma the second-youngest world champion in the division's history.

Instead, his inexperience began to show as his Croatian opponent - an Olympic bronze medallist whose only previous professional defeat came against Daniel Dubois - survived everything Itauma threw at him before completing a remarkable turnaround.

Hrgovic - wearing the red and white checks of his country - made his entrance first to a wall of boos, before the mood inside the O2 Arena flipped as Itauma emerged to a huge roar - taking his time and soaking up the reception.

The crowd had made its allegiances clear after a fiery build-up which included Itauma shoving Hrgovic, the Zagreb man slapping him back and plenty of verbal sparring.

Itauma came out with real intent, landing straight lefts from his southpaw stance. Hrgovic is known for his durability but struggled to keep pace with the Briton's speed early on.

Early in the second, a right hook knocked Hrgovic off-balance and his glove touched the canvas. Oasis star Noel Gallagher and boxing legend Prince Naseem Hamed were among those watching as the crowd gasped at almost every Itauma punch, whether it landed or not.

But by the end of the third, Itauma - who had boxed just 26 professional rounds before his first world-title fight - was already breathing heavily.

There had also been questions over his chin, simply because it had never really been tested. Hrgovic began landing the occasional heavy shot but Itauma took them well and fired straight back.

A fight in the crowd momentarily took attention away from the action in the fifth before an Itauma uppercut in the closing seconds brought the focus back to the ring.

Itauma continued to fire combinations but Hrgovic was barely budging. A huge right landed on the bell in the sixth and another followed in the seventh, yet the Croatian simply walked through them.

The Briton was well ahead but, rather than box his way towards victory, he continued to chase the knockout. A flurry in the eighth backed Hrgovic on to the ropes and had him in trouble, but Itauma was grimacing between exchanges and looking increasingly spent.

The youngster somehow stayed upright but his legs had gone. Hrgovic continued to press and when Itauma slumped into his corner, exhausted and barely able to defend himself, referee Howard Foster waved off the contest as the towel came in.

Hrgovic admitted he had been "outboxed" but leaves London as Croatia's first heavyweight world champion, with Frank Sanchez waiting as the IBF mandatory challenger.

A unification fight could follow, with Daniel Dubois holding the WBO title and set to face Fabio Wardley again in October.

For Itauma, this was supposed to be a coronation.

Instead, he leaves the O2 Arena with questions over whether the step up came too soon.

He has time to rebuild and there will be a strong feeling that, with a little more experience, this night could have ended very differently.

Londoner Dubois was stopped by Joe Joyce as an unbeaten 23-year-old before going on to become a two-time world champion. Itauma has even more time on his side.

"He's an amazing fighter," Hrgovic said. "I am the present. He is definitely the future."

Promoter Frank Warren suggested Itauma was carrying a leg injury in the final round but backed him to return.

"Moses gave everything," he added. "He has to go back to the drawing board and he can come again."

The expectation around Itauma will not disappear entirely overnight but the aura of invincibility has gone.
